title: The Unfinished Building on Ngong Road Where Lancet Kenya Began
conflicts: Slate year 2007 is wrong: all sources give 2009 (first call from Lancet's chairman in 2008, by Kalebi's account). Slate funding 'bootstrapped' is wrong: Kalebi says Lancet Laboratories of South Africa funded it and made him partner and CEO; he held a minority stake (7.67% of PLK per Business Daily 2021), though the Standard called him the largest single shareholder after the 2019 Cerba deal; recorded as 'mixed', story says minority stake. Business Daily 2021 says he grew 'the group' to 100+ labs in 11 countries, but the Standard gives that as all of Cerba-Lancet Africa while his East African group covered four countries; story uses the July 2017 figure (about 40 branches, six accredited facilities) reported by both Business Daily and the Standard. Business Daily 2024 says he left in 2018 for a three-year sabbatical; the 2021 reports have him retiring as CEO on 30 April 2021; story follows 2021. SANAS accreditation 'within its first year' is Kalebi's own claim and is attributed to him.
notes: Mentions talQen once in the reflection (natural link: diagnostics and accreditation). Story relies mainly on Kalebi's own interviews (Business Daily 2014, 2017 and 2024; The Star). The Star URL is dated 2016 but the page shows 20 January 2019. The 2017 Biko interview's '16 more laboratories across 17 counties' and the 600+ staff in Nation 2019 are not used.
